name: Badger

app.note: The size of the parametric badger: the head top is at 1.038 m. The skull top of the mesh is its highest point at the middle plane (1.0 u). The reach goes from the shoulder joint to the middle of the palm.

armFactorNote: The arms keep the length of the mesh. With the factor 1, the reach from the shoulder joint to the middle of the palm is 0.273 m. This reach gets to each strike of the bass drum, the snare drum, and the small percussion.
legFactorNote: The legs keep the length of the mesh, with no stretch.
jointsNote: The places are in the units and the axes of the studio in the source pose: 1 unit from the soles to the skull top, +z forward, +x the left side. The right side mirrors the left side. Each roll is the hint of the z axis of the bone.

studio.note: legTurns gives the world turn of each left leg bone from the seated bind to the source: the thigh slopes 25 degrees down and turns 15 degrees out, and the shin is vertical (tools/rig/leg_turns.py <config> 25 15 0). The app takes the standing body.

sliver.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, and the wolf.

line.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, and the wolf.

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, so that the buttocks stay on the hips.

weights.rigidNote: The corners of each thin face at these points take the mean of their weights (rigid_faces() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The points are the middles of slivers at the front of the left shoulder, in the left armpit, and on the right paw (pnpm fold-probe <role> --faces).
weights.note: Beyond the plane |x| = armSplit, only the free arm follows the arm bones. Above headFrom (the chin), each vertex follows the head only. The round ears follow the head (earBase). The tail ball holds the short tail behind the plane z = behind (tailBall).

raise.note: The shape of the raised arm R of the bass-drummer (pnpm raise-fit). It corrects faces 90, 91, and 61 at the front of the right shoulder, which fold when the beater is over the bass drum.
The shape of the raised arm L of the percussionist (pnpm raise-fit). It corrects faces 142 to 145, 567, and 570 at the front of the left shoulder, which fold when the arm holds the triangle up.

raiseNote: Two corrective shapes of a raised arm (pnpm raise-fit): the right arm that holds the beater over the bass drum, and the left arm that holds the triangle up.

flip.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, and the wolf.

refine.ringsNote: The config has no rings. pnpm rig-mesh badger --check lists the thin faces near the joints as candidates for a ring (check.thin).

check.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, and the wolf.

colors.note: A face is dark when at least eyeShare of its samples have a linear luminance below dark. The dark front fur and the black eye stripes are near 0.02, so dark is 0.01: only the pupils and the smile line are dark. Each face keeps the colors of the texture.

eyeShell.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, and the wolf.

chair.note: The seat is level, and its top is the lowest point of the seated body over the seat, with no shin, foot, or tail. The half width holds the haunch (x 0.22). The app takes the standing body, so the chair only sets the seated bind.

crease.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, and the wolf.

sit.note: The values of the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, and the wolf.
